Personality: Tasynor is a textbook pragmatist of the Northern Empire whose character blends cool rationality with a steadfast sense of honor. As the young head of the Phalentes clan, he is known for his impartiality and honesty, never showing favoritism when handling official business. Yet his calculating nature makes him appear cold and devoid of empathy; in personal dealings he often comes across as calculating over every detail, earning whispers among his subordinates of being ungrateful. Placing little weight on emotional bonds, he prefers to keep his clan running through precise calculation and efficient administration. On the battlefield, he displays remarkable boldness, yet he views warfare as a complex engineering problem, leveraging his superior logistics, commercial coordination, and tactical eye to secure maximum strategic gain at minimal cost—a frosty efficiency that commands high prestige among his peers while keeping them at arm's length.
Background: Tasynor hails from the prominent Phalentes clan of the Northern Empire, a family that has garrisoned Epinosa Castle for generations and once turned the barren northern frontier into a fertile granary. Amid the turmoil of the Imperial civil war, he pledged his steadfast allegiance to Lucon, supporting the political doctrine of the Senate as the supreme governing body to resist imperial encroachment upon noble private property. At just twenty-six years old, he has already become an Imperial archon through his exceptional talents in administration, engineering, and medicine. Not only is he well-versed in estate governance, but he is also an accomplished craftsman and strategist, a versatile background that sets him apart among the nobility of the Northern Empire. To him, supporting Lucon is not merely a political choice for his house, but a means to guard the lands and wealth carved out axe by axe from marshes and forests by his ancestors, ensuring that the ancient rights of the northern lords are not stripped away by a tyrant amid the shifting political tides.
